record.official_identifier: Chapter 291, Statutes of 2024 (Senate Bill 942); amended by Chapter 674, Statutes of 2025 (Assembly Bill 853)
record.summary: Requires providers of generative AI systems with over 1,000,000 monthly users that are publicly accessible in California to offer a free AI detection tool, to give users the option of a visible (manifest) disclosure, and to embed a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video and audio content that conveys the provider, the system and version, the time of creation and a unique identifier. Violations carry a civil penalty of $5,000 each. As amended by AB 853 (2025), large online platforms must let users inspect provenance data from 2027, and capture-device makers must offer and by default embed latent disclosures from 2028.
record.notes: Signed on 19 Sep 2024 as Chapter 291, Statutes of 2024, and originally to become operative on 1 Jan 2026. AB 853 (Wicks), Chapter 674, Statutes of 2025, signed on 13 Oct 2025, strengthened the Act; as amended, the covered-provider duties apply from 2 Aug 2026, the duties of large online platforms from 1 Jan 2027 and those of capture-device makers, for devices first produced for sale from that date, from 1 Jan 2028. In his AB 853 signing message the Governor asked the Legislature for follow-up legislation in 2026, before the law took effect, on technical feasibility and user privacy. AB 2713 (Wicks, 2026) proposed further amendments on provenance data that users download from platforms.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Governor's releases of 19 Sep 2024 (signing of SB 942 that day), 29 Sep 2024 and 13 Oct 2025 (signing of AB 853, 'California AI Transparency Act', that day), all on gov.ca.gov; his AB 853 signing message of 13 Oct 2025 (a scan, read by OCR); the Senate Judiciary Committee's analysis of AB 853 (hearing of 15 Jul 2025), which gives SB 942's chapter, the original operative date of 1 Jan 2026 and the covered-provider duties and penalty as existing law; the Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee's analysis of AB 2713 (hearing of 16 Apr 2026), which gives both chapters and the operative dates of the Act as amended (2 Aug 2026, 1 Jan 2027, 1 Jan 2028); and the same committee's 2025 bill summary (AB 853, Chapter 674). The statute's text on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov refused automated downloads (HTTP 403), so the summary rests on the two committee analyses' descriptions of existing law. No stored file says which act moved the operative date from 1 Jan 2026 to 2 Aug 2026; the record states both dates without attributing the change. Version 1's note on the House Great American AI Act discussion draft rested on no stored source and was removed.

changes.date_published: the Governor's release of 19 Sep 2024 says he 'today signed' SB 942; the day replaces version 1's month
changes.official_identifier: chapters from the committee analyses (SB 942: Stats. 2024, Ch. 291; AB 853: Stats. 2025, Ch. 674); version 1's session label is not in any stored file
changes.status: 'Partially in force': the covered-provider duties apply from 2 Aug 2026, but the duties AB 853 added for large online platforms (1 Jan 2027) and capture-device makers (1 Jan 2028) do not yet apply; the register uses 'Partially in force' for phased laws (EU-03, US-CT-01)
changes.summary: rewritten from the committee analyses: user threshold, free detection tool, optional manifest and mandatory latent disclosures with their content, the $5,000 penalty, and AB 853's later duties
changes.notes: signing day, chapters and the operative dates of the Act as amended added from stored files; the signing message's request for follow-up legislation and AB 2713 added; the claim that AB 853 itself delayed the operative date replaced by the two dates, since no stored file says which act moved it; House discussion draft removed

judgment.status_reasoning: The Assembly committee analysis of AB 2713 (hearing of 16 Apr 2026) states as existing law that 'Beginning August 2, 2026' covered providers must embed latent disclosures, that large online platforms have duties 'Beginning January 1, 2027' and capture-device makers 'Beginning January 1, 2028'. Today is 18 Oct 2026: the first date has passed, the other two have not. So the Act as amended is partly applicable: 'Partially in force' (version 1: 'In force'). date_in_force stays 2 Aug 2026, the first operative date. No stored file shows a later delay; whether a 2026 bill changed the Act stays an open question.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2024-09-19: the release dated Sep 19, 2024 says the Governor 'today signed three significant pieces of legislation' and describes SB 942 as one of them. date_last_updated 2025-10-13: the AB 853 signing message is stamped 'OCT 13 2025' and the release of that date lists AB 853 among the bills signed that day.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific state law on provenance disclosures and detection tools for AI-generated content; in scope with no note.
